title: Haitians and Afro-Cubans
summary: Haitians came to cut cane and return home; Machito says minor trades were left to blacks and compares to Jewish holidays in New York.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I see. Okay. Macho, what about the Haïtians? How did they get along with the Afro-Cubans?
Well, the Haitians they had no way out since they are black, so they went out there with the purpose just to cut the cane and come back to Haiti.
Okay. I know that the Haitians, which are French, of French descent, a lot of them settled in Santiago de Cuba in Oriente.
La Lupe, Benny More , they are of French descent, a lot of them learned how to speak Spanish and a lot of them became great Afro-Cuban musicians; so then the regular

and carpenter and dressmaker, all the minor things, what they consider minor things, that it was poor pay. We was the ones to - they used us for that, things, the same way they use here in New York. If it wasn't for the Jewish people here, the day that they had a holiday nobody work.
